input.quote: In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.1 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
input.rationale: Section 14.2.1 requires PB (our party) to pay SFJ a fixed sum equal to 300% of Development Costs if SFJ terminates for PB's uncured material breach, and Section 14.4.2 states that the amounts payable on a given termination are \"in lieu of any claim for damages\" — i.e., a breach-triggered liquidated amount payable by the customer, and a treble multiple is punitive rather than compensatory. That fails both the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount). Our edit changes only the operative payment words so that no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by PB on that termination, leaving the purchase and exclusive-remedy mechanics intact. We have not flagged the 300% at-will amount in Section 14.2.2 or the 150% change-of-control amount in Section 14.2.6, which are addressed under the termination-for-convenience and assignment rules; the parallel amounts in Sections 14.2.5.2, 14.2.7 and 14.2.10 should be conformed if this change is accepted. Section 14.4.2's cap on SFJ's damages claim benefits us and is not challenged.

ops.oldText: PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination
ops.newText: PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, no liquidated damages or penalty in respect of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the termination payment measured by 300% of Development Costs with an express statement that no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by PB, since a fixed sum triggered by termination and treated under Section 14.4.2 as in lieu of damages is a liquidated amount payable by us. If a payment is unavoidable, we could accept a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
proposal.summary: Section 14.2.1 amended so that PB pays no liquidated damages or penalty on SFJ's termination.

mappings.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer.
